content.text:
## Summary

**Defects found:**
1. **Broken tab order (WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order)** — Every form control had an explicit positive `tabindex` (`3, 1, 2, 5, 4`) that scrambled keyboard navigation into `last-name → email → first-name → book → party-size`, completely out of sync with the visual reading order (`first-name → last-name → email → party-size → book`). Positive `tabindex` values are also flagged by axe-core's best-practice ruleset.
2. **No reinforced focus indicator** — the page relied entirely on browser-default outlines with no explicit style, which is fragile across browsers/themes.

**Fixes applied (`index.html`):**
- Removed all `tabindex="…"` attributes from the two name inputs, email, party size, and the submit button. Since the DOM order already matches the visual layout, natural tab order now flows correctly without any tabindex hacks.
- Added an explicit `:focus-visible` outline (`3px solid #8c3b2e` with offset) for inputs and the button, using the page's own brand/accent color so the indicator is clearly visible (well over 3:1 contrast against both the white card and the off-white body) and stays true to the existing palette.

**Left alone:**
- All elements were already native (`label`+`input`, `<button type="submit">`), so no ARIA retrofitting was needed — Enter/Space activation, form submission, and label association all work natively.
- No dialogs or custom widgets exist on this page, so focus-trap/inert requirements don't apply here.
- Verified text color contrast (`p.sub` ~7.2:1, `.note` ~5.5:1, button text ~7.6:1) — all comfortably pass AA, so no palette changes were needed.
- `data-track` attributes, `id`s, and the instrumentation script are untouched.

The page now has a reading-order-matching tab sequence, native keyboard activation, and a clearly visible focus indicator on every interactive element, with no other WCAG 2.1 AA issues present in this simple, all-native form.
